title: XLOOKUP: exact match, no column counting

screens.prompt: In B6, return the price of the SKU in A6 with XLOOKUP, whose third argument is the answer column itself rather than a column number.

hints.syntax: =XLOOKUP(A6,A2:A5,D2:D5): the answer column goes in the third slot.
hints.func-xlookup: Three arguments: the SKU, the SKUs, the prices. XLOOKUP pairs them row by row.
hints.require-ref: Read the SKU from A6, so another product is one cell away.
hints.value: C2:C5 holds cost, so it answers 4.8. D1:D4 starts a row high, so its third price is 14. The third SKU needs the third price.
hints.error: #VALUE! means the two ranges are different sizes. #N/A means A6's SKU was not in the range you gave.

reject.why: the right answer with the older function
the right answer in the older two-function shape
two arguments, so there is no column to return from
the SKU typed into the formula instead of read from A6
the cost column instead of the price column, so 4.8
the return range one row off, so the third price becomes the second
lookup range pointed at the product names, so TX-103 matches nothing
a return range one cell longer than the lookup range
a lookup range that stops before TX-103

docs.explain:
XLOOKUP reads two ranges side by side. TX-103 is the third entry of A2:A5, so the answer is the third entry of D2:D5, which is 9.5. The cost column between them plays no part.

The third argument is the answer column itself, D2:D5, not a number. That is why the cost column can sit between the keys and the prices, and why pointing at C2:C5 returns 4.8 instead. The two ranges must be the same size, and each key must sit beside its answer.

D1:D4 starts one row too high and returns 14, because its third price is really the second. Match mode defaults to exact, so the last two arguments can stay empty.

errors.text: The SKU is not in the lookup range, which happens when the range stops early or points at the product names.
The lookup and return ranges are different sizes, so a price has no SKU to pair with.

docs.atWork: Price lists and rate cards where the key and the value are not neighbours, or where someone will reorder the sheet next week.
docs.outcome: Return a value from a column anywhere in the table, with no column number to count.
docs.dataset: SKU price list with cost and price columns

seo.title: XLOOKUP in Excel: exact match, no columns
seo.description: XLOOKUP reads a key column and an answer column in parallel, so inserting a column cannot break it. The third SKU returns 9.5, not the 4.8 cost beside it.
